sections.html:
Just south of the city of Albany, Bethlehem is an Albany County town where a sale touches two offices. Town Hall in Delmar holds assessments and building records, and the Albany County Clerk takes the deed. The 2025 estimate is 35,684 residents in 14,722 households, and 73.0% of those households own.

The typical owned home is valued at $370,400. Monthly owner costs are about $2,300 with a mortgage and $959 without, against a median rent of $1,721. Longtime owners tend to hold a lot of equity in a house that still has its original systems. A house needing a roof, kitchen or heating system can still sell on the open market, though showings and repair talks come first. A cash buyer skips those steps and prices in the work.

Bethlehem covers 49.03 square miles on the Hudson River side of the county, and U.S. Route 9W passes through it. Its communities are organized as hamlets.

  • Delmar: the most populous hamlet. Delaware Avenue holds the town hall, police station, justice court and public library, and the Four Corners intersection of Delaware and Kenwood avenues is the traditional center.
  • Elsmere: home to Delaware Plaza, a shopping plaza built in the 1950s with a large supermarket.
  • Slingerlands, Glenmont, Selkirk, South Bethlehem and North Bethlehem: the other hamlets, with ZIP codes of their own for most of them.

The Albany County Helderberg-Hudson Rail Trail, a paved path toward Albany, follows the old rail line through Delmar. Elm Avenue Park, the town's largest park, has pools, courts and winter skating, with swimming limited to residents and their guests. Parks and trails belong in a listing, because buyers ask what is nearby.

sections.h2: How to check your assessment before selling
sections.html:
Start online. Use the Town of Bethlehem's Beacon portal. It shows property data kept by the Assessor's Office, including structure details, exemptions, sale history, tax bill and payment information, and it lets you run comparable assessment and sales searches. The portal carries the 2026 final assessments.

Spot an error in the inventory, say the bedroom count or square footage? Send the portal's feedback form so the Assessor can fix it. A tidy record helps the buyer's appraisal and heads off closing surprises.

To contest an assessment, get the grievance form from the New York State tax department site or the Assessor's Office. Homeowners may file directly with the Assessor at any time before or on Grievance Day. Call the Assessor's Office for the date, since it follows the assessment calendar. Write the date down and give it to the buyer, because a challenge filed in time can lower the bill they inherit.

The Building Division, part of the Department of Economic Development and Planning, handles permits and zoning information. It sits in Room 214 of Town Hall at 445 Delaware Avenue in Delmar. Before a sale, ask that office whether any permit on your house is still open.

  • A permit is required for additions, alterations and demolition, and also for decks, fences, hot tubs, pools, porches, ramps, roofing, sheds, generators and signs.
  • Residential permits typically take 7 to 10 business days, and work should not start until the permit is issued. Commercial permits average 14 to 21 business days.
  • Inspections must be requested at least 24 hours ahead.
  • Zoning rules sit in Chapter 128 of the Town Code, and specific zoning requests such as legal uses should be made in writing.

For a project you finished years ago, ask whether the final inspection was ever signed off. Fixing that now takes a phone call and an inspection request made at least 24 hours ahead, while fixing it after a buyer's attorney spots it can hold up a closing. The division's records are public. Open permits show up there, so close out old ones before listing.

sections.h2: Selling a house with an accessory apartment
sections.html: An accessory apartment needs a Special Use Permit from the Planning Board under Section 128-73 of the Zoning Law, except in Rural Districts. If your house has a second unit, confirm it was approved before you list, because a buyer's attorney will ask. Ask the Planning Department for your permit record, and tell any buyer, including a cash buyer, what the approval covers.

Deeds for Bethlehem property are filed with the Albany County Clerk on Russell Road in Albany, indexed by liber and page number. Deeds and mortgages filed after 1980 can be searched through the clerk's website. Surveys are kept there too, filed by the map and drawer numbers printed on the deed.

The seller covers the state transfer tax of $2 per $500 of price. A buyer purchasing a residence at $1 million or more adds an extra 1%. Hand Form TP-584 to the county clerk along with the deed, and pay within 15 days of delivery. If one side skips its share, the other is exposed, so confirm both at closing.

Build a short folder before you talk to any buyer or sign a listing agreement. Print your Beacon record and mark errors. Ask the Building Division about open permits. Locate the deed, noting its liber and page, plus the survey's map and drawer numbers. Add your lender payoff letter and newest tax bill.

Your title company will ask for the same papers, so having them ready saves days. A second unit adds its Special Use Permit to the pile. Cash buyers appreciate the folder too, and a clean one speeds up the offer: it lets them price the house accurately instead of padding for unknowns.

sections.h2: Your options if you want out of a Bethlehem house
sections.html:
You can hire an agent, sell it yourself or take a cash purchase. A listing tends to show the biggest number on paper but brings showings, inspection requests and a closing that depends on the buyer's lender.

Cash fits an inherited Slingerlands house nobody wants to clear out, a Selkirk rental with tenants, or a Delmar home with more repairs than its owner wants to handle. The buyer takes it as is and the closing follows your calendar. Weigh each offer against your net after repairs, agent costs and carrying costs, and test it against Beacon sale history for nearby parcels.

faqs.q: Is a certificate of occupancy required when my Bethlehem house sells?
faqs.a: Ask the Building Division before you list, since it keeps the permit records. It can say whether a project such as a deck or finished basement has an open permit or a missing sign-off.

faqs.q: Where is a Bethlehem deed recorded?
faqs.a: The county, not the town. Albany County Clerk files deeds by liber and page, and deeds and mortgages after 1980 can be viewed online. The TP-584 goes in with the deed.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Bethlehem assessment?
faqs.a: Submit the state grievance form to the Town Assessor's Office by Grievance Day. Compare similar properties and sales on the Beacon portal first. Hiring someone is optional.

faqs.q: Which side owes the state transfer tax in a Bethlehem closing?
faqs.a: The base tax of $2 per $500 falls on the seller. The extra 1% on residences at $1 million or more falls on the buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bethlehem house that has an accessory apartment?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the apartment was approved. Outside Rural Districts the Planning Board must have granted a Special Use Permit, and the Planning Department can show you the record.
